B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP price or MCP-specific limits were found in the official materials reviewed. Access requires a Zuora tenant with Zuora AI enabled and OAuth authorization.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Zuora pricing depends on products, scope, transaction volume, business model, regions, and implementation needs; the vendor directs buyers to request a commercial proposal.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Official FAQ describes product and scope-based pricing but gives no amounts or MCP-specific per-call price.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Tenant AI must be enabled by an organization administrator. Tenant permission mode controls access: Read-Only prevents write actions; Read-Write permits write actions subject to the external MCP client's behavior. OAuth authorization and the authorizing user's product permissions apply.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and OneID organization administrator; user permissions and tenant configuration also constrain access. The MCP client controls whether it prompts for write approval.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Zuora API"` and a JSON error stating `Missing Bearer token` (code `90000011`). The protected-resource document for the endpoint origin returned resource `https://api.zuora.com`, authorization server `https://one.zuora.com`, scope `mcp-server`, and bearer method `header`. The path-suffixed protected-resource URL returned HTTP 404. The authorization-server document advertises authorization_code, client_credentials, and refresh_token grants; PKCE S256; client authentication methods client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, client_secret_jwt, private_key_jwt, and none; and client ID metadata document support. No registration_endpoint or token lifetime is present in the supplied metadata.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official list classifies tools as Read, Write, or Mixed. No MCP tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are published. 2. Zuora states it cannot enforce the Zuora AI product's per-action approval step for external MCP writes; approval depends on the calling client. 3. OAuth scope is `mcp-server`; remote access inherits the authorizing user's permissions. OneID tenant AI permission controls Read-Only or Read-Write. Multi-Org access follows integration-user org permissions; Multi-Entity authorization selects an entity. OAuth metadata lists grants and revocation/introspection endpoints but no token lifetime. 4. Docs list regional production and sandbox URLs; tenant modes include Read-Only. No URL toolset/filter or query-free parameter documented. 5. Documentation says access follows tenant/user permissions and selected org/entity; field masking or MCP-specific PII exclusion is not documented. 6. MCP-specific rate limits, quotas, result caps, truncation, and per-call charges not found. 7. Input schemas and validation/correction behavior not published. 8. MCP-specific logging, auditing, and telemetry details not found. 9. `submit_mcp_feedback` submits confirmed MCP feedback; no rating/survey tool listed. 10. Official resources provide task guidance; the reference recommends asking built-in AI about tool usage. The docs do not establish server-enforced behavior for those recommendations. 11. Server-side memory or behavior-dependent tool changes not documented. 12. Flat official tool list; remote and local variants are documented as supporting the same operations, with endpoints varying by region/environment. 13. No general raw REST/API execution tool appears in the official list; `zuora_graphql` is classified Read and described for GraphQL exploration and queries.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Use the built-in AI capabilities to explore the server's available features and tools. For example, ask "What can I do with the manage_workflow tool?" You can also request guidance on using a specific tool or Zuora feature, such as "Give me five useful prompts for working with invoices."
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The official reference presents one flat list of 91 tools. Zuora also documents regional/environment endpoints and local/remote variants, but says the local and remote servers support the same operations.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference lists 91 tools and states that they cover 330+ operations; the full list is in actions.json. The supplied endpoint host api.zuora.com is absent from the official regional endpoint table, but the endpoint path is /mcp and its OAuth metadata identifies it as a protected Zuora resource; the official /mcp reference is the best available tool list. No catalogue-only actions were added. APIs.io lists a different endpoint, https://developer.zuora.com/mcp, without a Zuora tool list; Pipedream's page is a proxy page with tools not loaded in the captured copy. No catalogue count for this endpoint was available.

E_aggregated.token_method: Hosted server definitions and initialize instructions were not available verbatim; the public repository is a coding-agent plugin, not the hosted server code.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: NOT FOUND: the reviewed sources do not provide a complete comparison of all human product operations against MCP-exposed operations. MCP tool names describe broad subsets, and exact tool schemas were not published in the tool reference.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The reference encourages using built-in AI to explore tools and ask for guidance. External MCP write approvals are client-dependent; Zuora says it cannot enforce the in-product per-action approval step for external MCP actions.
F_documentation.governance_promises: AI Commitments state: "Zuora and the AI Providers will not use Customer Data to train, re-train, improve, or fine-tune any AI models." It also states: "Customer Data will not be transferred outside of the Customer’s approved AWS data center."
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The server overview says remote access inherits permissions of the authorizing user along with tenant-level Zuora AI permission. Zuora's AI approach describes transparency, privacy, and security principles.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance and tenant-level modes are documented as access controls. External write approval is explicitly left to the MCP client. AI Commitments provide vendor-level data-use and residency commitments, but the reviewed MCP documentation does not expose implementation details that independently verify these controls at tool-call level.

contradictions: The supplied endpoint is https://api.zuora.com/mcp, while Zuora's official endpoint guide lists regional and sandbox /mcp hosts but not api.zuora.com. No endpoint-specific tool list was found, so the documented official /mcp tool list is used as best-available evidence.

The official tool reference describes 91 tools and 330+ operations, while the supplied endpoint's OAuth scope metadata advertises only `mcp-server` and does not enumerate individual tool permissions. The scope cannot be mapped to the listed read/write classifications from available evidence.
observations_for_research: Zuora exposes tenant-level Read-Only and Read-Write modes. Its documentation distinguishes approval in Zuora's own AI experience from third-party MCP client approval.
The official tool reference names `submit_mcp_feedback` and describes it as submitting confirmed feedback for the MCP server.
Zuora documents regional production and sandbox endpoints, but the supplied global-addressed host is not present in its endpoint table.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, pages/INDEX.txt and captured official pages, tool-reference text, scripts and HTML, local repository, commit metadata, and plausibility report. The repository is the official Zuora Coding Agent plugin; its .mcp.json invokes a separately installed zuora-mcp@latest package, and the hosted implementation is not present there. Tool schemas, hosted initialize instructions, exact protocol version, and endpoint-specific tool list were not found. APIs.io describes developer.zuora.com/mcp, a different endpoint; Pipedream is a proxy listing with unavailable action details. Unofficial third-party Zuora MCP projects were present in links.json and were not used as evidence.
